newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close firmer but futures pressuring.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close firmer but futures pressuring.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed only marginally firmer on Monday after late selling pressure appeared, due mainly to the rise in the futures market.
The general index rose 0.48 points, 0.13 percent, to 372.75. The Ibex-35 leading share index gained 4.95 points, 0.12 percent, to 4,271.25.
Telefonica was up 15 pesetas to 2,445 with more than three million shares traded. Repsol also gained 15 pesetas to 4,425 with 650,000 shares exchanging hands.
Traders said performance had been mixed and noted that there had been some profit-taking in afternoon trade, but added this was not a cause for concern.
"The market saw some selling pressure at the end of the day, but the mood is quiet and it doesn't look like there will be an important correction," said a trader.
Dealers did not exclude a further drop on Tuesday but said the bourse was likely to track overseas markets.
Volume was in line with recent sessions at 36.1 billion pesetas, with large firms soaking up most of the trade.
Banco Popular performed best among large banks, up 1.95 percent, while BBV was up one percent. Popular, Argentaria, Santander, Banesto and BCH all cut their prime rates on Monday.
